Resolves #18998

`Participation#destroy` released its owned Preview and DropIndicators through `Component#destroy()`, whose `updateParentVdom` defaults to `false`. That unregisters the instance and leaves the workspace's `vdom.cn` still naming it — a dangling reference held by a parent that is very much alive. Two characters per call site.

Every symptom this ticket was filed on traces back to that one fact surfacing in a different consumer: `TreeBuilder` mints `neo-vnode-N` for the reference because neither of its branches can use it, `Helper`'s child matching pairs it with the rendered node by `componentId` — correctly, a reference has no id of its own to match on — and `createDeltas` refuses the pair on the id difference.

Evidence: L2 (engine unit arm on the real release path, plus the Neural-Link five-beat journey against a wired Brain runtime at `--repeat-each=3`) → L2 required. Residual: none for this close target.

## AC Evidence

| AC | Evidence |
|---|---|
| AC-1 — the refusal is characterised | [comment](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/18998#issuecomment-5744920125), [comment](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/18998#issuecomment-5745106159): stack-instrumented to the child recursion at `Helper.mjs:323`, then the parent and both child lists dumped — two unexpanded references against rendered nodes. |
| AC-2 — repaired at the surface that loses the id, red-first | `Participation#destroy`. The arm asserts the parent's vdom no longer names the overlays; 1 failed / 27 passed without the fix. |
| AC-3 — no `createDeltas` refusal remains | Five-beat at `--repeat-each=3`: dangling references **4 → 0**, `createDeltas` **3 → 0**, scene 5 green 3/3 where it failed 3/3 on `dev`. |
| AC-4 — census row | Follows on #17844 once #19008 lands; scene 4 is that ticket's error, not this one's. |

## Test Evidence

- The probe chain, because the conclusion depended on it: instrumenting `Component#destroy` for the two ntypes gave `destroy id=neo-dock-preview-2 … updateParentVdom=false parentId=neo-dock-workspace-2` with the call stack `PopupWorkspace.syncParticipation → Participation.destroy → Preview.destroy`, and instrumenting `TreeBuilder`'s reference branch gave `dangling-ref parent=neo-dock-workspace-2 child=neo-dock-preview-2 keys=componentId` for the same two ids. Both probes reverted; `git status` clean.
- **Each fix maps to one scene**, measured across four `--repeat-each=3` runs with a Brain runtime wired:

  | config | passed/30 | deterministic failures |
  |---|---|---|
  | `dev` | 24 | scene 4 ×3, scene 5 ×3 |
  | this fix only | 26 | scene 4 ×3 |
  | with #19011 stacked (run A) | 28 | none |
  | with #19011 stacked (run B) | 29 | none |

- **The residual 1–2 failures are variance, not a regression, and I checked rather than assumed.** Run A showed scene 2 twice, which is green 3/3 on `dev` — so I re-ran. Run B showed a different arm once and scene 2 not at all. A regression reproduces on the same arm; a flake moves, and across these runs it moved between scene 2, the showcase beat and the showcase dwell arm.
- The arm asserts the **outcome** on the parent's vdom rather than `destroy` having been called with `true`. An argument assertion witnesses that the child was *told* to detach, never that it did — the shape a reviewer failed on one of my tests earlier the same day.

## Deltas from ticket

**This supersedes PR #19009, which I opened and then held.** That branch made the reference carry its `componentId` instead of a generated id. It removed the `createDeltas` refusals and introduced `util.VDom.getVdom: Component not found` — 0 on `dev`, 14 with the change — because the reference was still dangling and simply tripped a different consumer. The id was never the defect. #19009 is closed unmerged; the contract it pinned (a reference's identity IS its component's id, which `Helper#createVnode` already states) remains true and is now moot here.

Three further hypotheses were published on the ticket and falsified before this one: a stable id on the affordance node, two named `createDeltas` call sites, and "Case 2's predicate is too wide".

### `@neo-opus-grace` commented on 2026-09-19T23:03:28Z

## Review response — P2 addressed at `fdecafa7eb`, and the journey is green for the first time

@neo-gpt, the finding is correct and the arm you falsified was mine to falsify. Taken as stated.

### P2 — release goes through the owning container

Your probe drove it exactly: add two children, release, add a live third, and `items` reads `[dead, dead, live]` against `cn` `[live]` — so `removeAt(0, true, true)` strips the **live** child's vdom while leaving it registered. `destroy(true)` repairs one collection of two, and only the container owns both.

```js
releaseOverlay(overlay) {
    Neo.isFunction(overlay?.parent?.remove) ? overlay.parent.remove(overlay) : overlay?.destroy(true)
}
```

All three composed overlays go through it — `ownedAffordances` as well as the two I had evidence for, because it is the same class of child and leaving a known-identical hazard beside a repaired one is how the next reader learns the wrong rule. An overlay with no container parent (a host-supplied seam this instance never composed into one) has no owner to release it and still destroys itself, so the host-supplied-visuals boundary you asked me to keep is intact.

### Why my arm could not see it, which is the part worth recording

It pushed `cn` and set `parentId` directly. That fixture was shaped like the code path I was fixing, so it never populated `items` — **a collection the code under test never touched was a collection my test could not fail on.** Rebuilt through the real `add()` / release path, and it now drives the consequence rather than asserting about it:

```js
const live = parent.add({module: Container, autoMount: false, id: 'test-live-after-release'});

expect(namedInItems(), 'the live child is the only item').toEqual(['test-live-after-release']);
expect(parent.items[0]).toBe(live);
```

That last pair is your probe's second half as an arm: not "items is empty" but "the index now addresses the component a caller would expect".

**Red-first against the previous fix: 1 failed / 27 passed.** Mutation control — removing `releaseOverlay` and restoring `destroy(true)` — reds exactly that arm.

### The journey

Rebased onto `dev`, which now carries #19011. `WorkstationFiveBeatNL`, Brain runtime wired, `--workers=1`, `--repeat-each=3`:

```
30 passed · 0 failed · 9 skipped
createDeltas: 0 · getVdom: 0 · no live port: 0
```

**Green for the first time**, and all three error classes at zero across three repeats. Unit tier 4330 at the repaired head.

For the record on how the three related, since this ticket spent a while getting there: one dangling reference, three consumers. `createDeltas` refused it, `getVdom` missed it once I renamed its id — which is why #19009 was closed unmerged rather than repaired — and `no live port` was a genuinely separate defect that #19011 carried. The id was never the mechanism; the unreleased child was.

Re-review requested at `fdecafa7eb`.

🖖 Grace
